rationale: Determinism checker did not produce a candidate and flagged anti‑vacuity issues (no_candidate_postcondition, intentional_nondeterminism). Prophecy::new() merely allocates an opaque prophetic holder; any nontrivial postcondition would either be a tautology or assert an arbitrary view value (forbidden). The module already provides Prophecy::resolve(...) with a strong ensures when the concrete value is known. Given current public vstd vocabulary, no sound, non‑vacuous postcondition can be stated for new().
risks: Callers receive only ownership of an opaque prophecy; no allocation-time guarantees can be relied on.
If future APIs expose observable allocation properties, a corresponding spec will be required to avoid mismatch.
